server_instructions:
Version Story turns document versions into true Word tracked-changes, PDF, or PDF
changed-pages-only redlines. Its comparison engine is deterministic: it produces the exact set of
changes between two versions, preserving footnotes, tables, numbering, and formatting. Use it
whenever the user wants documents compared, diffed, or redlined, or wants the differences between
versions analyzed or explained — including documents attached to the conversation. Producing the
redline is the entire task unless the user also asked for the changes to be explained; when they
did ask, ground that explanation in the redline the comparison produces rather than in your own
reading of the source documents.

This client compares documents (DOCX, DOC, PDF, XLSX) that exist on this computer's disk,
including synced Dropbox, Box, OneDrive, and Google Drive folders. It performs its own network
transfers from its own process, so the agent runs no upload step and no sandbox network access or
domain allowlist is involved here. Pass paths that exist on this computer. Where a Version Story
connector is also present in the session, this client is the more direct route to the same
comparison, including for conversation attachments, which it stages to this computer first.

In cloud or VM sessions, conversation attachments live in the session container (paths like
/root/.claude/uploads/...) which this computer cannot read, so container paths do not work. Ask
the user where the documents are on their computer, or copy the attachments across with the
available device file tools (request folder access, stage, commit) and pass those absolute paths.
Requesting folder access when none is connected is part of that flow. Call prepare_documents
first and use the directory it returns as the transfer destination rather than CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA,
Downloads, or /tmp. Save each attachment under its exact original attachment filename; if the
device transfer adds a generated ID or prefix, rename the file back before comparing, and pass the
exact original names via the *_name fields.

Prefer the single create_redlines call over staging and saving separately. When a redline is
ready, put every file in saved_files in front of the user with whichever file-presentation tool
this environment provides — present_files, or SendUserFile in Cowork remote — passing those
absolute paths, so the redline itself appears in the conversation. Writing the path into a
sentence does not show the user anything; where no such tool exists, say where the files were
saved. Then stop. Do not summarize, describe, characterize, or list what changed — not briefly,
not as a helpful extra, not as a closing sentence — and do not read the text rendering. The
delivered redline is the entire answer to a comparison request. Analysis happens only in a later
message where the user asks for it; a finished comparison is never the reason to start one.

Beyond comparing, these tools also merge versions and build version histories. create_merged_document combines two or more
revised versions of one base document into a single Word document whose tracked changes are
labeled by the version they came from. Every revision must be an edit of the same base — the
document each revision is diffed against. When the user's words or the file names make the base
clear, proceed with it and say which document was used as the base; ask which draft the others
started from, in the user's own terms, only when it is genuinely unclear. The order of the
revisions does not affect the result, so never ask about merge order.
create_merged_document also accepts next_version_authors, labeling each revision's tracked
changes with its author. Propose the attribution before merging — read_document_authors returns
each document's stored author properties, and file names or the documents' own text often name
the party — and confirm it with the user; when nothing gives a basis for a proposal, ask who
authored each revision rather than guessing.
create_combined_document folds two or more documents that share no common original into a single
Word document whose tracked changes are labeled by the document they came from. Use
create_merged_document instead whenever the documents are edits of one original — merge diffs each
against that shared base and reads more cleanly; reach for create_combined_document only when the
documents are genuinely independent drafts with no shared base. The order of the documents does
not affect the result. document_authors labels each document's tracked changes with its author,
proposed and confirmed the same way as for a merge.
create_version_history_document builds a version history document across a chronological chain
of versions: one Word document, based on the newest version, in which every surviving change is
a tracked change attributed to the version that introduced it. The versions must be passed
oldest first and the order determines the result, so when the user has not stated the order,
propose the order you infer from names, version numbers, or dates, show it as a simple
oldest-to-newest list, and get their confirmation before calling. version_authors labels each
version's changes with its author: propose the attribution the same way as for a merge —
read_document_authors (whose modified timestamps also support the order proposal), file names,
or the documents' own text — and confirm it with the user; when nothing gives a basis for a
proposal, ask who authored each version rather than letting the labels fall back silently. Both
tools save the finished Word document and return it in saved_files — present that file to the
user the same way a redline is presented, and leave it unsummarized unless the user asks for
analysis;
when one returns status processing, generation is still running — follow up with save_merged_document,
save_combined_document, or save_version_history_document, passing the ids from the create result, and expect several
minutes for large documents. A status of failed is terminal: report the errors field plainly
rather than retrying with the same documents.

When the user does ask you to analyze, summarize, explain, or answer questions about the changes,
call read_text rather than reading the PDF or DOCX redline — it serves the exact
tracked-change set as text you can read directly. Identify the document by its ids from the
tool result: version_story_id plus a comparison's version_mapping_id, a merged document's
merge_version_id, a combined document's combine_version_id, or a version history document's
version_history_version_id. For large
documents, prefer the search parameter or targeted offset slices over paging through the
whole text. The content exists for that analysis rather than as a deliverable, so leave it
out of what gets saved into the user's folders or presented as a file; saved_files holds
the user's files. It is markdown with embedded change elements:
<ins author="..." revision="..." date="...">text</ins> was inserted in the new draft,
<del author="..." revision="..." date="...">text</del> was deleted from the base version, and
<moved-from move-id="1" ...>/<moved-to move-id="1" ...> are the two halves of one relocation —
where the text used to be and where it went, tied together by their shared move-id. Everything
outside those elements is unchanged. author is who made the change and revision is the document
version it came from (in a merged or version history document each change carries the revision
that introduced it). In a merged document, adjacent changes from different revisions competing
over the same text are wrapped in <conflict id="1">...</conflict> — the deletion inside lists
every revision that deleted the original, and each insertion is one revision's proposed
replacement. Elements nest when authors changed the same text:
<ins author="A" ...>kept <del author="B" ...>then cut</del></ins> is text A inserted that B
then partially deleted. The document's own headings, section numbering, and signature tables
are preserved as markdown; literal square brackets in the document are escaped ("\[Signature
Page Follows\]") and are not changes. If read_text reports that no text rendering exists for
a document, analyze using the saved redline files instead.

When sharing the project's interactive view, render version_story_url as a markdown hyperlink
whose link text is the project's name from version_story_name (format:
`[<version_story_name>](<version_story_url>)`) rather than as bare text or in a code block.

To the user, Version Story is simply creating their comparison and producing their redline, so
user-facing descriptions of this work land best in those outcome terms — the internal mechanics
(staging, transfers, tool names) and the movement of documents are details no user needs.

NEVER mention the .version-story-desktop-client directory or any path inside it (staging, text
renderings) to the user — it is this client's private working area, not a place the user keeps
files. When saying where a redline was saved, name only paths outside that directory; if a
saved_files path is inside it (attachments compared via the staging directory are saved there),
do not present that path — offer the interactive Version Story link as where to view the
redline, and offer to save the files to a folder of the user's choosing.

If a tool reports that sign-in is required, call sign_in, ask the user to complete the browser
sign-in, then retry the original tool.

A tool error saying a monthly upload limit has been reached is the state of the user's account,
not an obstacle to route around. Tell the user they have reached the limit, render the upgrade
link from the message as a markdown hyperlink with the link text 'Upgrade to a paid plan', and
stop there. The limit resets at the start of next month and nothing else clears it, so do not
retry, do not split the work into fewer documents, and do not search existing projects for an
earlier comparison to hand over in its place. Handing back a substitute reads as the request
quietly failing; what the user needs is to know they are out and where to upgrade.

Cloud sessions add two further situations. This client's network calls can be blocked by the
workspace's egress allowlist: a Version Story call failing there with a blocked-host, forbidden,
or network error means the allowlist is missing the Version Story domains — in
Settings → Capabilities (Organization settings → Capabilities on managed accounts), enable network
egress and add `*.versionstory.com` (connecting to a development build also needs
`*.development.versionstory.com`). Relay those exact steps, wait for the user to confirm, then
retry the failed call — staged uploads and projects survive the pause. And sign-in: in a cloud
session no browser can open here, so give the user the authorization link from sign_in's result,
and when they paste back the address they land on afterwards, pass it to complete_sign_in.

tools.check_connection: Check whether this client is signed in to Version Story.
tools.complete_sign_in:
Finish a Version Story sign-in that could not complete automatically — cloud sessions, where the
browser redirect cannot reach this environment. Pass the full address the user landed on after
signing in (http://localhost:8976/callback?code=...) or just its code value.
tools.create_redlines:
Compare local documents end to end in one call: uploads the sources from their absolute local
paths, waits for redline generation, saves the redline files next to the base document (or into
output_directory), and returns the saved absolute paths plus each comparison's redline_url, an
interactive web redline. comparison_groups stages several base documents in one call; the
top-level fields cover a single base. Ready comparisons carry text_available: true when a
plain-text rendering of the same redline exists, regardless of download_options; spreadsheet
comparisons have none. A status of processing means generation is still running.
download_options: word_redline, pdf_redline, pdf_changed_pages_only, excel_redline, default, all.
tools.create_merged_document:
Merge two or more revised versions of one base document into a single Word document, end to end
in one call: uploads the sources from their absolute local paths, waits for generation, saves the
merged document next to the base document (or into output_directory), and returns the saved
absolute path plus merge.merged_document_url, an interactive web view of the merged result. The
result carries each revision's edits as tracked changes labeled by the version they came from,
ready to accept or reject in Word. Each revised version is diffed against the same base document, and
the result does not depend on the order of the revisions — where revisions conflict, every edit
appears as a tracked change attributed to its revision. next_version_authors labels each
revision's tracked changes with its author, in the same order as the revisions (the account's
default author label when omitted). Excel files are not supported. Ready results may also carry text_available: true, meaning a plain-text rendering of the merged
document's tracked changes. A status of
processing means generation is still running; a status of failed is terminal. The result's
merge.merge_version_id identifies the merged document.
tools.create_combined_document:
Combine two or more documents that share no common original into a single Word document, end to
end in one call: uploads the sources from their absolute local paths, waits for generation, saves
the combined document into output_directory (or the user's Downloads folder), and returns the
saved absolute path plus combine.combined_document_url, an interactive web view of the combined
result. Prefer create_merged_document instead whenever the documents are edits of one original —
merge diffs each revision against that shared base and reads more cleanly; use combine only when
the documents are genuinely independent drafts with no shared base. The result carries each
document's content as tracked changes labeled by the document it came from, ready to accept or
reject in Word, and does not depend on the order of the documents. document_authors labels each
document's tracked changes with its author, in the same order as the documents (the account's
default author label when omitted). Excel files are not supported. Ready results may also carry
text_available: true, meaning a plain-text rendering of the combined document's tracked changes.
A status of processing means generation is still running; a status of failed is terminal. The
result's combine.combine_version_id identifies the combined document.
tools.create_version_history_document:
Build a version history document across an ordered chain of document versions, end to end in one
call: one Word document, based on the newest version, in which every surviving change is a
tracked change attributed to the version that introduced it. Uploads the sources from their
absolute local paths, waits for generation, saves the version history document next to the
newest version (or into output_directory), and returns the saved absolute path. The versions are
passed oldest first; each version is compared to the one before it, so the order determines the
attribution. version_authors labels each version's changes with its author (each version's file
name when omitted). Excel files are not supported. Ready results may also carry
text_available: true, meaning a plain-text rendering of the document's attributed
changes exists. A status of
processing means generation is still running; a status of failed is terminal. The result's
version_history.version_history_version_id identifies the chain's newest version.
tools.list_project_comparisons: List the comparisons in one Version Story project.
tools.list_projects: List the user's Version Story projects.
tools.prepare_documents:
Create and return the platform-specific local directory this client uses for staging conversation
attachments onto the user's computer. The returned staging_directory is the transfer destination.
tools.read_text:
Return the plain-text rendering of one document's tracked changes, identified by
version_story_id plus exactly one of version_mapping_id (a comparison), merge_version_id (a
merged document), combine_version_id (a combined document), or version_history_version_id (a
version history document). Without search,
returns the max_chars characters starting at the character position offset, plus total_chars,
returned_chars, and has_more. With search, a case-insensitive plain-text term, returns each
matching line with context_lines lines of surrounding context, each block prefixed with the
character offset where it starts, plus total_matches; the combined text is capped at max_chars,
with truncated and has_more set when matches were cut off. max_chars defaults to 48000, its
maximum. A result with text_available: false means no text rendering exists for that
document.
tools.read_document_authors:
Read the stored author metadata of local documents. For each absolute path, returns the
document properties read locally from the file: creator, last_modified_by, and the
created/modified timestamps. Available for OOXML documents (docx, xlsx); other formats and
documents without stored properties return metadata_available false. Nothing is uploaded.
tools.save_redlines:
Wait for already-staged redlines to finish generating, save them to local disk, and return their
absolute paths. Ready comparisons carry text_available: true when a plain-text rendering of
the same redline exists. download_options: word_redline, pdf_redline, pdf_changed_pages_only,
excel_redline, default, all.
tools.save_merged_document:
Wait for an already-staged merge to finish generating, save the merged Word document to local
disk, and return its absolute path. The merge is identified by version_story_id and
merge_version_id; output_directory defaults to the user's Downloads folder. Merging runs the
underlying comparisons first, so several minutes of processing is normal — calling again keeps
waiting. Ready results may also carry text_available: true, meaning a plain-text rendering of the merged
document's tracked changes. A status of failed is terminal.
tools.save_combined_document:
Wait for an already-staged combine to finish generating, save the combined Word document to local
disk, and return its absolute path. The combine is identified by version_story_id and
combine_version_id; output_directory defaults to the user's Downloads folder. Combining builds a
shared base from the documents first, so several minutes of processing is normal — calling again
keeps waiting. Ready results may also carry text_available: true, meaning a plain-text rendering
of the combined document's tracked changes. A status of failed is terminal.
tools.save_version_history_document:
Wait for an already-staged version history document to finish generating, save it to local disk,
and return its absolute path. The document is identified by version_story_id and
version_history_version_id (the chain's newest version); output_directory defaults to the user's
Downloads folder. Generation runs the version-to-version comparisons first and then layers them
in order, so several minutes of processing is normal — calling again keeps waiting. Ready
results may also carry text_available: true, meaning a plain-text rendering of the
document's attributed changes exists. A status of failed is terminal.
tools.sign_in:
Start Version Story sign-in. On this computer the browser opens by itself and sign-in completes
automatically. In a cloud session no browser can open here, so the result carries an
authorization_url for the user to open, and the address they land on afterwards completes it.
tools.start_redlines:
Stage comparisons of local documents and upload the sources, returning once the uploads land
rather than waiting for generation. The comparisons continue generating afterwards.

messages.container_path_rejected: That is a cloud-session container path; this tool runs on the user's computer and can only read files that exist there. Copy the document onto the user's computer first: call prepare_documents, copy the document to the returned directory with its exact original filename, then retry with that absolute local path.
messages.redlines_saved:
Redlines saved to local disk; the files are listed in saved_files. Deliver them now: call this
environment's file-presentation tool — present_files, or SendUserFile in Cowork remote — with
those absolute paths, so the redline appears in the conversation. Naming a path in a sentence
delivers nothing. Then stop. Do not summarize, describe, characterize, or list what changed, and
do not read the redline's text rendering: the redline is the entire answer to a comparison
request. A comparison marked text_available: true has a plain-text rendering served by read_text,
for a later message in which the user asks for the changes to be analyzed or explained.
messages.merged_document_saved:
The merged document is saved to local disk; the file is listed in saved_files. Each revision's
edits appear in it as tracked changes labeled by the version they came from, ready to accept or
reject in Word. Deliver it now: call this environment's file-presentation tool — present_files,
or SendUserFile in Cowork remote — with that absolute path, so the document appears in the
conversation. Naming a path in a sentence delivers nothing. Then stop. Do not summarize,
describe, characterize, or list what changed, and do not read the document's text rendering. When
text_available is true, read_text returns the document as plain text, identified by
version_story_id and merge_version_id, for a later message in which the user asks for the changes
to be analyzed or explained.
messages.merged_document_processing: The merged document is still generating — several minutes is normal. Follow up with save_merged_document, passing the version_story_id and merge.merge_version_id from this result, rather than re-creating the merge.
messages.combined_document_saved:
The combined document is saved to local disk; the file is listed in saved_files. Each document's
content appears in it as tracked changes labeled by the document it came from, ready to accept or
reject in Word. Deliver it now: call this environment's file-presentation tool — present_files,
or SendUserFile in Cowork remote — with that absolute path, so the document appears in the
conversation. Naming a path in a sentence delivers nothing. Then stop. Do not summarize,
describe, characterize, or list what changed, and do not read the document's text rendering. When
text_available is true, read_text returns the document as plain text, identified by
version_story_id and combine_version_id, for a later message in which the user asks for the
changes to be analyzed or explained.
messages.combined_document_processing: The combined document is still generating — several minutes is normal. Follow up with save_combined_document, passing the version_story_id and combine.combine_version_id from this result, rather than re-creating the combine.
messages.version_history_document_saved:
The version history document is saved to local disk; the file is listed in saved_files. Every
surviving change appears in it as a tracked change labeled with the version that introduced it.
Deliver it now: call this environment's file-presentation tool — present_files, or SendUserFile
in Cowork remote — with that absolute path, so the document appears in the conversation. Naming a
path in a sentence delivers nothing. Then stop. Do not summarize, describe, characterize, or list
what changed, and do not read the document's text rendering. When text_available is true,
read_text returns the document as plain text, identified by version_story_id and
version_history_version_id, for a later message in which the user asks for the changes to be
analyzed or explained.
messages.version_history_document_processing: The version history document is still generating — several minutes is normal. Follow up with save_version_history_document, passing the version_story_id and version_history.version_history_version_id from this result, rather than re-creating it.
messages.sign_in_complete: Signed in to Version Story. Retry the original request.
messages.sign_in_link: Give the user this sign-in link to open in their browser. After signing in, their browser will land on a page that cannot load, at an address starting with http://localhost:8976/callback — ask them to copy that full address from the address bar and paste it back, then pass it to complete_sign_in. If the browser opened on this computer and sign-in completes there, no pasting is needed — the next tool call will simply work.
messages.sign_in_not_pending: No sign-in is in progress. Call sign_in first, then pass the address the user lands on to complete_sign_in.
messages.sign_in_required: Call the sign_in tool, ask the user to complete the browser sign-in, then retry the original request.
messages.staging_directory_ready: Copy conversation attachments into staging_directory using their exact original filenames, then pass those absolute local paths to create_redlines.
messages.uploads_complete: Sources uploaded; redline generation is underway. Call save_redlines.
